visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 more accurately visualizes the projectile setup with a ground-level parabolic trajectory, velocity components, flight-time derivation, and correct use of v0y=20 m/s, while Lesson 1 mostly shows Desmos equation entries with warning icons and no plotted trajectory or range representation at the midpoint.

interactivity.rationale: Lesson 2 includes a well-formed, wired fill-in checkpoint after act_decomposition with a real prompt, accepted answer, hint, and remediation path, whereas Lesson 1 has no available gate specs or plan and therefore no functioning interactivity.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 2 has clear, natural narration with appropriately spoken math terms, while Lesson 1 contains awkward repetition and an unrelated trailing line ('A golfer hits a ball') that makes the audio feel defective.

sync.rationale: Lesson 2 provides mostly intentional cue offsets that generally align with the narrated references, despite a few early or late triggers, whereas Lesson 1 has no beat/timing data or cue information at all, making its visual-narration synchronization unverifiable and effectively unsupported.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 correctly and clearly builds the projectile-motion solution through component decomposition, vertical flight time, and horizontal range calculation, whereas Lesson 1 mostly reports a Desmos endpoint without explaining the equations or derivation and even ends with irrelevant/confusing narration.

polish.rationale: Lesson 2 has a clean, centered, visually consistent full-frame layout with readable text and uncluttered panels, whereas Lesson 1 is dominated by browser chrome and platform controls, has off-center content with lots of empty space, and includes distracting chat/overlay UI elements that make the presentation feel cluttered.

aggregator.explanation: All six dimension agents strongly favored Lesson 2, with high confidence across visual accuracy, interactivity, narration quality, synchronization, concept accuracy, and polish. Lesson 2 was judged to provide a correct projectile-motion visualization, functional checkpoint interactivity, clearer narration, better visual-narration alignment, more rigorous conceptual derivation, and a cleaner presentation. Lesson 1 lacked functional interactivity and timing data, showed weaker or incomplete visuals, had awkward/irrelevant narration, and appeared cluttered or underdeveloped. The unanimous high-confidence verdicts make Lesson 2 the clear overall winner.
